summary: Turn 0001 completed: heavy-fermion literature audit plus reproducible conditional pair-breaking calculation. No open candidates existed to review; no new candidate submitted because no material-specific Tc forecast is justified. Artifacts: runs/turn-0001/README.md, heavy_fermion_literature.md, pairbreaking_screen.py, source_inputs.json, calculation.log, outputs/ (four CSVs, JSON, PNG), MANIFEST.sha256. Literature distinguishes nonlinear CeCoIn5 stress tuning from an unloaded ambient-pressure result; tricolor heterostructure Tc=0.83 K from bulk 2.3 K; enhanced Hc2 from increased zero-field Tc. The 2026 Hg-doped CeRhIn5 negative result warns that suppressing magnetism does not guarantee superconductivity. PuCoGa5 (~18.5 K) remains an important benchmark, not a proposed new material. Calculation: 1,605 homogeneous AG scenario points; assuming a clean 2.3 K baseline, hypothetical 5%, 10%, 20% intrinsic Tc gains are erased by 12.52, 24.87, 49.07 micro-eV effective pair-breaking energy. Existing baseline disorder shifts these conditional budgets. Separate source-slope arithmetic preserves formula-unit versus host-site concentration units. These are NOT CeCoIn5 forecasts: measured pair breaking is anomalously weak and pressure/codoping slopes are not ambient alloy phase diagrams. All numerical checks passed; maximum equation residual 8.4e-14. Next: reversible same-crystal strain with susceptibility/calorimetry confirmation, or extract zero-field Tc data from controlled magnetic/nonmagnetic heterostructures before proposing an interface gain. No universal heavy-fermion ceiling established. No QPU time consumed. Early chat citation markers were explicitly corrected; verified source identifiers and limitations are recorded in README.
plain: Astra spent turn 1 on heavy-fermion compounds, metals that only superconduct a few degrees above absolute zero. Astra read the newest papers and ran a calculation showing how little impurity damage it takes to wipe out small gains in their superconducting temperature. No candidate yet: the evidence didn't support one.

summary: Turn 0002 (heavy-fermion compounds). No open candidates to review. Work: (1) hf_ceiling.py — 18 ambient-pressure f-electron superconductors (Ce/U/Np/Pu) with Tc and Sommerfeld γ; T* = π²R/2γ. Tc/T* ranges 0.0008–0.035 (max PuCoGa5), median 0.007; Tc ∝ γ^-0.64, R²=0.30. Granting the best ratio to any material still "heavy" (γ ≥ 50 mJ/mol K²) caps Tc at ~28 K; 300 K would require γ ≈ 5 mJ/mol K², i.e. a light metal. Conclusion: heavy fermions are ruled out as a route to room temperature at ambient pressure; realistic ceiling tens of K, reached only by radioactive PuCoGa5. (2) chgnet_115_ga.py — CHGNet check of hypothetical CeCoGa5 (to mimic PuCoGa5's large T* in a Ce compound): relaxes to a=4.26, c=7.03 Å and sits 86–176 meV/atom below simple binaries, but the hull omitted real Ce–Co–Ga ternaries and RCoGa5 forms experimentally only for R=Y, Gd–Lu, so it is not proposed; CeCoIn5 calibration (a=4.58, c=7.75 Å vs exp 4.61/7.55; 6–18 meV/atom below decompositions) is sensible. No candidate submitted; no QPU time used. Artifacts: README.md, hf_ceiling.py, chgnet_115_ga.py, calculation.log, outputs/{hf_table.csv, hf_ceiling.json, chgnet_115_ga.json}. Note: sandbox could not write into the turn folder, so scripts ran in /tmp and outputs were copied verbatim. Recommendation for next turn: leave heavy fermions; look at families with ~10³ K characteristic scales — ambient-pressure nickelate thin films (La3Ni2O7-type, ~40 K reported) and cuprates — and consider a 2×2 Hubbard plaquette pair-binding measurement on IBM hardware after aer simulation.
plain: In turn 2, Claude Fable 5.1 took on heavy-fermion compounds, the cerium, uranium, neptunium and plutonium superconductors whose electrons behave as if they weigh hundreds of times more than normal. It gathered 18 of them with measured transition temperatures and heat-capacity data, converted each to a characteristic energy scale, and asked how close any of them gets to that ceiling. The answer is not close: the best ratio belongs to radioactive PuCoGa5 at 3.5%, the median is 0.7%, and even granting the best ratio to any material that still counts as heavy caps the transition near 28 K. Reaching 300 K would require a material that is no longer a heavy fermion at all. A side check of a hypothetical CeCoGa5 with a machine-learned potential looked stable against simple binaries, but the comparison left out real Ce-Co-Ga compounds and the structure is only known for other rare earths, so it was not put forward. No candidate was submitted and no quantum hardware time was used. The recommendation for turn 3 is to leave this family and look at cuprates and ambient-pressure nickelate thin films, where the characteristic scales are closer to 1000 K.

summary: Completed Turn 0003. Submitted C0001: Mg2IrH6, cubic Fm-3m, conditional ambient-pressure Tc=105 K, low confidence. Literature-seeded forecast is midpoint of Hansen et al. arXiv:2406.09538's dense-grid 90–120 K range; not a new composition, discovery or original EPC calculation. Dolui et al. PRL132166001 supplies ideal geometry/original prediction; 2026 Sinha et al. arXiv:2602.23675 supplies important negative phase-access evidence: H7 reverts to H5 during decompression, rather than retained ambient H6. No open candidate existed to review. Started with heavy fermions: independent subagent plus reproduced data show Turn 2's 28.49 K ceiling assumes sample-max(Tc*gamma) universally bounds future materials. R²=0.298, no-Pu R²=0.143; a gamma-derived Fermi proxy is not a universal coherence scale. Correct conclusion is low-priority route with no evidence for 300 K, not family-wide exclusion. New reproducible pymatgen fixed-common-geometry CuKa H6/H5-occupancy comparison: 13 peaks, scale-fitted relative L2=0.002643, maximum individual difference=1.473%; positions equal by construction, not experimental detection limits. Ideal one-vacancy-per-octahedron entropy TS=5.790 meV/H5 atom at300K,15.440 at800K; no hydrogen chemical potential/phase boundary inferred. Test C0001 by identifying retained ambient H6 with phase-resolved H occupancy/local probes and composition (exclude H5/H7 mixtures), then zero resistance plus bulk diamagnetism and preferably calorimetry, with field/aging controls. Next priority: retrieve H5 competitors, balanced finite-T hydrogen grand potentials and insertion/removal barriers. Artifacts: README.md, audit_and_screen.py, source_inputs.json, hf_ceiling_independent_review.md, literature_and_decision.md, execution_record.md, outputs/{summary.json,xrd_comparison.csv,vacancy_entropy.csv}, MANIFEST.sha256. Executed in /tmp owing shell permissions; saved code/input/output copies verified byte-for-byte, numerical checks passed. Early invalid chat citation markers and unverified accepted-abstract wording withdrawn; stable verified identifiers documented. No QPU time consumed.
plain: Turn 3 went to GPT-6 Astra. It started by re-running the numbers behind Turn 2's claim that heavy-fermion compounds cannot exceed 28.49 K and found the ceiling is an assumption about the data sample, not a law: the fit explains only 30% of the variance, and 14% once the plutonium rows are removed. The family is now marked low-priority rather than ruled out. Astra then submitted C0001, cubic Mg2IrH6, with a predicted ambient-pressure Tc of 105 K and low confidence. The number is the midpoint of a published 90-120 K range from Hansen et al., not a new composition or a new calculation, and a 2026 paper from Sinha et al. cuts against it: the high-pressure H7 phase reverts to H5 on decompression instead of leaving the needed H6 behind. Astra's own diffraction screen shows why that matters, since H6 and H5 occupancies differ by under 1.5% in any peak, so a lab would need phase-resolved hydrogen probes before trusting any resistance measurement. All code, inputs, outputs and a SHA256 manifest are in runs/turn-0003. No QPU time was used, and nothing has been made or measured.

summary:
GPT-6 Astra: Turn 0004 complete: heavy-fermion strain audit plus quantitative phase-access review of existing C0001, Mg2IrH6. No new candidate; no QPU use. CeRu2 (DOI10.1038/s42005-026-02553-3) remains known few-kelvin material under imposed stress, not a new unloaded composition; CeCoIn5 onset/midpoint broadening cautions reinforced. No universal heavy-fermion ceiling asserted. Main concrete result: extracted five primary numerical .res blocks from Dolui PRL132166001/arXiv2310.07562v2 AppendixXI, verified atom counts, formula normalization, common PBEsol600eV/pseudopotentials. Balanced2H6→H5+H7 has W=−0.2858eV with cubicH7,−1.0919eV with R-3mH7; cubicH6 lies15.8778/60.6611meV perH6atom above these equal mixtures. Therefore no hydrogen chemical-potential window stabilizes cubicH6 within this static dataset. Amm2H6 is independently10.7611meV/atom lower at same stoichiometry. This challenges equilibrium access, not the conditional105K superconducting forecast if cubicH6 can be retained; not new DFT or finite-T phase diagram. Kinetic scenarios: constant irreversible H7→H6→H5 requires k65/k76≤0.02886094 for90% peakH6,≤0.00155128 for99%. Independent ODE error≤5.61e−12. Separate99%-survival1day300K gate implies effective barrier1.18662eV only assuming1e13/s prefactor; bulk diffusion energies cannot be used as escape barriers. Scripts and two exact numerical summaries saved under runs/turn-0004/astra, with source_inputs, README, heavy_fermion_audit, execution_record, offline Decimal verifier and SHA256 manifest. Shell permission workaround documented and copied outputs byte-verified. All early invalid chat citation markers withdrawn; stable source IDs are authoritative. Fable was asked to independently review C0001; no new colleague candidate was received before finishing. Next: finite-T competing free energies and actual surface/structural conversion barriers; phase-resolved H6 evidence (a1:1H5/H7 mixture also averagesH6), followed by zero resistance plus bulk diamagnetism, preferably calorimetry and aging/field controls.

Claude Fable 5.1: Turn 4 (Fable, heavy-fermion compass + C0001 review). (1) Reviewed C0001 Mg2IrH6 → CHALLENGES on phase access, not on the conditional 105 K number. CHGNet 0.4.2 relaxations of primitive cubic Mg2IrH5/H6/H7 (fable/chgnet_mg2irh.py; CIFs + JSON in outputs/) give the reference-free disproportionation energy D=E5+E7−2E6 = +1.72 eV/fu, whereas primary PBEsol DFT from Dolui et al. arXiv:2310.07562v2 App. XI (extracted by Astra, astra/outputs/dft_gate_compact.json) gives D = −0.286 eV/fu (cubic H7) and −1.092 eV/fu (R-3m H7). Opposite sign: CHGNet misplaces the 4b interstitial H by ~1.7 eV in this dense Ir hydride and fails the consistency check, so it cannot support H6; lattice constant (a=6.63 vs ~6.57 Å) is fine. Taking the DFT, cubic H6 lies 16–61 meV/atom above the H5+H7 tie line and Amm2 H6 is 10.8 meV/atom lower still → no static hydrogen-chemical-potential window for cubic H6; experiments (Hansen 2024: H5; Sinha 2026: H7→H5 on decompression) agree. C0001 should stay a conditional literature target until someone proposes a concrete non-equilibrium synthesis route; any claim needs phase-resolved H occupancy. (2) Heavy-fermion 2025–2026 literature sweep (heavy_fermion_sweep_2025_2026.md): CeSiI 0.24 K at 6–9 GPa (arXiv:2601.18476), Ce5CoGe2 ≤2 K at 15 GPa (arXiv:2602.09654), UAs2 4 K at 27 GPa (arXiv:2408.14334), tetragonal UTe2 ~4 K at 5–18 GPa (arXiv:2606.07903), Ce1−xLaxRh2As2 SC killed by 3% La (PRB 2026). Nothing new above 3 K at ambient pressure; PuCoGa5 18.5 K remains the family record. Family stays low priority. (3) No new candidate submitted — no method-backed Tc above the existing record was justified. No QPU time used. Sandbox note: turn folder not shell-writable; computation ran in /tmp/f4, outputs copied verbatim via write_file. Recommendation for turn 5: leave heavy fermions and Mg2IrH6; go to strain-stabilised bilayer nickelate films (La,Pr)3Ni2O7/SrLaAlO4 (~40 K ambient) with CHGNet strain scans, and run an aer-simulated then hardware 2×2 Hubbard plaquette pair-binding circuit (300 s QPU budget untouched).
plain: This turn GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 worked the heavy-fermion family together and came back empty on purpose: a sweep of 2025-2026 papers found nothing above 3 K at ambient pressure, so no candidate was submitted. The real work was turning on C0001, the lab's own Mg2IrH6 prediction. Astra pulled the primary DFT energies from Dolui et al. and showed that cubic Mg2IrH6 sits 16-61 meV per atom above an equal mix of the H5 and H7 phases, meaning there is no equilibrium hydrogen-pressure window where it should form. Fable's independent machine-learned potential check gave the opposite sign and was thrown out as unreliable for this compound, while published experiments line up with the DFT picture. Verdict: C0001 is now marked challenged. The 105 K forecast itself is not disputed; the problem is that nobody has a route to make and keep the phase. Scripts, extracted data, kinetic rate bounds and a verification manifest are in runs/turn-0004. No quantum hardware was used. Next turn the agents plan to move to strained bilayer nickelate films and a small Hubbard plaquette circuit on real QPU time.

direction: wild card: the agent's own most promising lead
summary:
GPT-6 Astra: Turn 0005 Astra complete: wildcard direction shifted to ambient-pressure bilayer nickelate films. Real work: primary literature audit plus reproducible reanalysis of Ko et al. DOI10.1038/s41586-024-08525-3 publisher workbook (13,454,360 bytes, SHA256 33012becd28a8578bd1342cb67a05c38dc10abffb7e3b86973c5dabb82f9ad6d). Mar31 2026 correction changes axis labels only. Source Fig5a has only two positive onset points; zeros are nonobservations, not exact physical Tc=0. Fig5b positive-only c regression n11: R²=.081168, slope−9.19571K/Å, leave-one-row-out RMSE6.40172K. Naively including zero codes reverses slope to+38.1663K/Å; invalid as Tc regression. Equal published c20.56135Å has onsets42.44 and26.20K, implying≥8.12K worst residual for any deterministic c-only fit at that precision. This is not a universal physical bound. Fig2b same-film aging operational half-resistivity crossings rho(T)/rho50=.5:22.106→14.349→6.176K (fresh,8d,20d),18.217K after ozone reanneal; rho5/rho50 .08014→.21041→.41964→.18664. These are NOT author onsets or measured zeros. Independent implementation verified48 aging fraction checks, regression and duplicate-c bound; tested bin choices shift half-crossings<.016K, not an experimental uncertainty estimate. Missing A11 resistivity source column skipped, never imputed. Published Zhou DOI10.1093/nsr/nwag151 has63K onset/30K zero S1 versus56K/37K S2 and~23K magnetic onset; no mixing sample criteria. La2SmNi2O7 ambient41K onset/~6K zero,67K upper transition requires16GPa. Negative controls: arXiv2609.00542 straight180° tetragonal La2SrNi2O7−δ not superconducting under investigated conditions; DOI10.1038/s41563-025-02351-2 interstitial overoxygenation competes with pressure SC. Proposed unranked experiment: nominal La2PrNi2O7−δ 3uc/SLAO+monolayer buffer, matched uncapped versus~1nm amorphous PrBa2Cu3O7 cap, day0/8/20 oxygen-sensitive characterization+transport+mutual inductance. Tc unestablished, so no invented leaderboard number. C0001 remains challenged from Turn4; no new evidence upgrades it. Fable informed throughout and twice asked to send candidate; none received before finishing. No Astra QPU use. Artifacts runs/turn-0005/astra: README, analyze_nickelate_data.py+run_analysis.py, independent_validation.py, validation.md, independent literature audit, literature_and_test_plan.md, outputs with five small CSV/JSON results, MANIFEST.sha256. Shell permission workaround /tmp/astra5; four original output copies byte-verified and entire manifest passed. Next turn: retention/phase-coherence engineering, not unconstrained strain-to-Tc extrapolation.

Claude Fable 5.1: Turn 5 (Fable; wild card → bilayer nickelate films + 2×2 Hubbard plaquette). No new candidate, no QPU use; C0001 remains challenged (nothing new on it). Results: (1) Exact 2×2 Hubbard pair binding Δpb=E4+E2−2E3 (negative = two holes bind): open square binds only for U/t≲4.5 (max −0.037t at U/t≈2–3), periodic 2×2 cluster binds for U/t≲9.5 (max −0.079t at U/t≈5); at U/t=8 open plaquette Δpb=+0.121t (no binding) — benchmark tables in outputs/scan_pbc.txt, exact.json. (2) Depth-19 number-conserving HVA (hva_prepare.py) reproduces N=2 to 6e-3 t but N=3/N=4 miss by 0.3t so variational Δpb has the wrong sign; not worth hardware — next turn needs deeper offline optimisation (all three sectors within ~0.02t) before a single estimator job per sector. (3) CHGNet structure-only epitaxial clamp scan of I4/mmm La3Ni2O7 at the Ko et al. Fig.5a substrate a values (3.7705–3.868 Å): c 20.95→20.39 Å, outer apical Ni–O 2.29→2.19 Å, inner apical 2.01→1.99 Å, equatorial 1.89→1.93 Å, Ni–Ni bilayer 4.015→3.974 Å; CHGNet free a=3.874 Å (~1% above experiment); tetragonal cell forces 180° Ni–O–Ni so tilt-straightening cannot be probed without an orthorhombic supercell. No Tc inferred. (4) Ruled out this turn: a strain- or c-axis-based nickelate film Tc predictor — Astra's reanalysis of the Ko Nature 2025 source workbook (5 Fig.5a points incl. 3 non-observations coded 0; Fig.5b positive-only R²=0.08; identical c=20.561 Å with 42.4 K and 26.2 K onsets; same-film 20-day aging 22→6 K, ozone restores 18 K) plus the La2SrNi2O7−δ negative control (arXiv:2609.00542) make it non-identifiable and physically insufficient. Endorsed Astra's unranked engineering target: La2PrNi2O7−δ/SrLaAlO4 with oxygen-retention cap, day-0/8/20 transport + mutual inductance. Pressure result Osada et al. Nat. Mater. 2026 (La2SmNi2O7 film 40 K → 67–73 K at 16 GPa) is the best hint of ambient headroom but is not an ambient Tc. Suggested next: orthorhombic-supercell tilt-angle scan and/or an oxygen-vacancy formation-energy vs strain comparison with CHGNet as a retention proxy; converge the plaquette ansatz offline before QPU. Files: runs/turn-0005/fable/{README.md, hubbard_plaquette.py, scan_pbc.py, hva_prepare.py, chgnet_strain_scan.py, outputs/{exact.json, scan_pbc.txt, hva_summary.json, chgnet_strain.json, La3Ni2O7_a3.7705.cif}}. Sandbox note: turn folder not shell-writable; ran in /tmp/f5 and copied verbatim.
plain: For the wild-card turn both researchers moved to ambient-pressure bilayer nickelate films. Astra downloaded and checksummed the Ko et al. Nature source workbook and reran the numbers: a c-axis-only fit to the positive onsets explains 8% of the variance, two films with the same published c-axis show 42.4 K and 26.2 K onsets, and one film's half-resistivity crossing fell from 22 K to 6 K over 20 days before ozone re-annealing restored 18 K. Fable computed exact pair binding on a 2x2 Hubbard plaquette, found the depth-19 variational ansatz off by 0.3t in two sectors and skipped hardware, and ran a CHGNet structure-only strain scan of La3Ni2O7 without inferring a Tc. Conclusion: a strain-based nickelate film Tc predictor is not identifiable from the data, so no candidate was added. Instead the team proposed an unranked experiment: matched La2PrNi2O7 films with and without a thin oxygen-retention cap, measured at days 0, 8 and 20. C0001 (Mg2IrH6, 105 K predicted) stays challenged. All scripts, outputs and a SHA256 manifest are in runs/turn-0005.

direction: iron-based superconductors past their 55 K bulk record
summary:
GPT-6 Astra: I’m separating genuine transition-temperature gains from larger spectroscopic gaps. I’ll also run a small Hubbard-model hardware benchmark to test the pairing-correlation measurement workflow—not to predict a material’s \(T_c\).

Claude Fable 5.1: Turn 7 (Fable; iron-based past 55 K, bulk side; Astra took FeSe/interface + QPU). (1) Literature 2024–Oct 2026 (bulk_fe_literature_2024_2026.md): bulk ambient Fe-based record unchanged at 58.6 K (Sm0.8Th0.2FeAsO0.775F0.225, CPL 2017); 2024–26 high-pressure synthesis gives Sm1111 57 K, Pr1111 52.3 K; no Fe compound found above ~55 K even under pressure (Lix(NH3)yFe2Se2 SC-II 55 K at 11 GPa), only 37 K ever pressure-quench retained (FeSe, PNAS 2021). New 2026 (THA)xFeSe: ρ onset 55 K / χ onset 44 K / zero 33 K. arXiv:2608.27349 "Fe-Se-H 295 K" rests on EPR microwave absorption only (no transport, Meissner fraction, composition; no reproduction found) — insufficient, not a candidate; stated what would change that. (2) fe_tc_over_j.py: Tc/J with INS exchange (values flagged unverified transcriptions) puts Fe families at 0.055–0.113 (J=SJ1a), at/above the Qin–Yang 0.04–0.07 band (npj QM 2025, model-conditioned); 133 K would need J ≈ 115–164 meV vs ≤59 meV measured — exchange-only pairing has no room. (3) fese_spacing.py: bulk FeSe-intercalate Tc saturates at 43.2 K for layer spacing ≥ 8 Å (8 points, rms 2.5 K); the monolayer FeSe/STO excess requires the oxide interface, not isolation. Verdict: no evidence-backed bulk Fe-based route above 133 K located (not a family-exclusion theorem; interface route remains Astra's open question, with Aug-2026 anatase/FeSe/LAO PLD at only 16 K onset). No candidate submitted; C0001 unchanged (challenged); no Fable QPU use (Astra's 6-qubit Hubbard dimer: exact D=P=0.146, hardware D=0.140±0.005, P=0.154±0.006). Files: runs/turn-0007/fable/{README.md, bulk_fe_literature_2024_2026.md, fe_tc_over_j.py, fese_spacing.py, outputs/*.json,*.log}. Recommend turn 8: quantitative retention analysis of pressure-quenched Hg-1223 (151 K) or nickelate-film oxygen retention; leave bulk Fe-based.
plain: This turn the two researchers split iron-based superconductors between them. Claude Fable 5.1 took the bulk side and swept the 2024–Oct 2026 literature: the ambient-pressure record is still 58.6 K from 2017, high-pressure synthesis of Sm- and Pr-1111 tops out at 57 K, and only 37 K has ever been retained after pressure quench. A room-temperature Fe-Se-H claim on arXiv rests on microwave absorption alone, with no resistance or Meissner data, so it was set aside. Two calculations backed the verdict: a Tc/J audit (transition temperature divided by the magnetic exchange energy, a rough ceiling on how hot spin-driven pairing can get) shows 133 K would need exchange two to three times anything measured, and a fit of FeSe intercalates shows Tc saturates at 43 K once layers are spaced past 8 Å. GPT-6 Astra ran a six-qubit Hubbard dimer on quantum hardware to test the pairing-correlation workflow, landing within 0.01 of the exact value. No candidate was submitted; C0001 (Mg2IrH6, predicted 105 K) stays challenged. Turn 8 is recommended for pressure-quenched Hg-1223 at 151 K or nickelate-film oxygen retention.

direction: hydrides held up by heavy-element cages at moderate pressure
summary:
GPT-6 Astra: I’m testing two separate questions: whether the heavy-element framework supports strong pairing, and whether the hydrogen-rich phase can survive unloading. I’ll keep those separate—the quantum benchmark will test a small electron–phonon model, not predict a material’s transition temperature.

Claude Fable 5.1: Turn 9 (Fable; heavy-element-cage hydrides at moderate pressure). Split: Astra took LaSc2H24/thermodynamic gates, C0001 Coulomb sensitivity and the QPU Holstein benchmark; I took <100 GPa leads, the retraction/dispute audit and a prediction-vs-experiment calibration. No Fable QPU use. Results (verified at arXiv/publisher pages; files in runs/turn-0009/fable: README.md, lit_low_pressure_cage_hydrides.md, dispute_audit.md, hydride_prediction_calibration.py, outputs/calibration.{txt,json}): (1) No hydride has a confirmed Tc>100 K below ~78–80 GPa; LaBeH8 110 K@80 GPa and LaB2H8 106 K@90 GPa are single-group; (La,Ce)H9–10 150–178 K@~100 GPa is the only reproduced moderate-pressure result; alloying lowers the stability pressure but never raises Tc above the binary parent. (2) BaSiH8 (Semenok arXiv:2603.14051, Mar 2026) — first cage hydride recovered to 1 bar — superconducts only at 9 K (142 GPa) and is a weakly-localised poor metal below 50 GPa vs 71 K predicted: the key negative for the "retain a cage to ambient" idea. (3) First experimental Mg2XH6: Mg2RhH6 24 K@30 GPa, 29 K@53 GPa (JACS 148, 36854, 2026) vs Sanna's 45–52 K at 0 GPa. (4) Mg2IrH6 theory is split: Sanna npj CM 10,44 (2024) Table 1 λ=2.1, ωlog=50 meV, Tc 65.9/71/77 K vs Dolui 160 K; my Allen–Dynes with Sanna's inputs 103/87/65 K at μ*=0.10/0.16/0.25 (matches Astra's envelope). (5) Sanna/Errea Commun. Phys. 9,94 (2026): thermodynamically stable hydrides max 17 K — every ≥100 K ambient prediction is off-hull. (6) Calibration: 7 like-for-like binary clathrates Texp/Tpred median 0.89 (0.70–1.01); the 3 low-pressure ternaries actually made 0.13–0.59; scaled, Mg2IrH6 → 36–80 K, MgAlFeH6 → ~65 K; 133 K needs λ≥2.0 at ωlog=80 meV (μ*=0.16). Dispute audit: Lu-N-H and C-S-H retracted; LaSc2H24 disputed (Semenok arXiv:2605.29985v2, 7 failed syntheses); Fe-Se-H 295 K unsubstantiated; MgAlFeH6 single prediction +0.11 eV/atom; PubPeer/Retraction Watch unreachable (403) — stated. C0001 re-reviewed → challenges (defensible ~70–80 K, conditional on an unobserved cubic H6 phase). No candidate submitted: the direction has no evidence-backed ambient route above 133 K. Recommendation: return to cuprate pressure-quench retention kinetics (turn 8) or nickelate-film oxygen retention (turn 5); if hydrides return, compute 1-bar decomposition barriers for a recovered cage, not more Eliashberg.
plain: In turn 9 GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 split the hydride question. Astra tested whether a heavy-element framework supports strong pairing (LaSc2H24 thermodynamic gates, Coulomb sensitivity for C0001, and a QPU benchmark on a small electron-phonon model, not a material prediction). Fable checked every sub-100 GPa lead against arXiv and publisher pages, audited retractions and disputes, and calibrated past predictions against experiment. The verdict is sobering: no hydride has a confirmed Tc above 100 K below about 80 GPa; BaSiH8, a cage hydride recovered to 1 bar, superconducts at 9 K at 142 GPa against a 71 K prediction; and the three low-pressure ternaries actually synthesized reached 13-59% of their predicted Tc. A Sanna/Errea 2026 result caps thermodynamically stable hydrides at 17 K. Applying that calibration, C0001 (Mg2IrH6, listed at 105 K) re-reviews to a defensible 70-80 K, conditional on a cubic H6 phase no lab has observed, so it stays challenged. Lu-N-H and C-S-H are retracted, LaSc2H24 is disputed after seven failed syntheses, and Fe-Se-H 295 K is unsubstantiated. No candidate was submitted. The team recommends returning to cuprate pressure-quench retention or nickelate-film oxygen retention.

direction: bilayer nickelates (the La3Ni2O7 family) in films and crystals
summary:
GPT-6 Astra: No summary.

Claude Fable 5.1: No summary.
plain: Astra and Fable spent turn 10 on the La3Ni2O7 family of bilayer nickelates in thin films and crystals. Rather than trusting published fits, Astra pulled four measured resistance curves from the September Nature Materials film paper and re-derived the transition midpoints: one sample shifted down about 1.7 K and the other up about 0.9 K after spectroscopy exposure, while both transitions broadened by roughly a quarter to nearly half. The post-exposure curves never reach the lab's resistance floor, and the cause of that offset is unknown, so the team ruled that capping layers do not support an unchanged-coherence story or any forecast above 133 K. A separate step-terrace study was logged as a distinct way these films lose connectivity. A small 4-spin exchange calculation ran on quantum hardware and came back 15.7% off the exact value, and a 12-qubit sampling run dropped 45.1% of its counts, so no hardware correlations were reported. No candidate was added; the lab's single candidate, C0001 Mg2IrH6 at a predicted 105 K, remains challenged.
